To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Ca2+-activated cation channel in SR vesicles has two binding sites for caffeine, one of which is a high-affinity site and the other a low-affinity one, while the channel has one binding site for procaine.
caffeine enhances the choline influx into the sarcoplasmic (SR) vesicle, and procaine inhibits the choline influx.
caffeine and procaine regulate the Ca2+-dependent cation channel of sarcoplasmic-reticulum vesicles in opposite manners.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinetic mechanism of the action of caffeine and procain on Ca2+-gating of the Ca2+ channel in SR vesicles.
the mechanism of caffeine action on the Ca2+ channel in the SR.
the kinetics of the actions of two drugs on the Ca2+ channel of SR vesicles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ca2+-dependent choline influx is inhibited by procaine and is enhanced by caffeine.

caffeine enhances the choline influx through the Ca2+-activated cation channel by increasing the affinity of Ca+2 for the receptor site, whereas procaine blocks the choline influx either directly by inhibiting the Ca2+-dependent opening of the channel or by inhibiting the channel opening enhanced by caffeine.
caffeine enhances the affinity of Ca for the Ca-receptor site of the channel, while procaine blocks the Ca-receptor channel by inhibiting the channel opening and closing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effects of caffeine and of procaine on the SR Ca2+-gating system were different in the following aspects: (a) Caffeine increased the affinity of Ca for the receptor site, whereas procaine blocked the channel by binding to an inhibitory site.

caffeine regulates the equilibrium between open- and closed-states of the Ca2+ channel, while procaine inhibits the Ca2+ influx by binding to the inhibitory binding site on the channel only in the open-state.

the Ca2+-activated cation channel in the SR membrane has three distinct binding sites, i.e., the receptor site for Ca2+ (Kd = 1 x 10(-7) M), the binding site for caffeine (Kd =1 x 10-4 M), and the binding site for procaine (Kd =4 x 10(-5) M).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Ca2+-dependent choline influx in the SR vesicles is regulated by the equilibrium between open- and closed-states of the Ca2+ gated cation channels, and the equilibrium is controlled by the binding of caffeine and procain to the Ca2+ receptor site and inhibitory site of the channel, respectively.
the Ca2+-dependent choline influx is regulated by the binding of caffeine or procaine at different sites.
the effects of caffeine and of procaine on the channel activity are quite different.
